Usage: gotools import-gobin [options] [binary...]

  Take over the Go tools you installed with 'go install'. Every Go binary
  records the package and module version it was built from; import-gobin reads
  that (it never runs the binary) and installs the same package@version into the
  project, under the binary's name, like 'install' does. The binary itself is
  not copied.

  With no arguments it only lists what is in the directory and what could be
  imported. Name the binaries to import, or pass --all for every importable one.
  The directory is GOBIN, else the first GOPATH entry's bin, unless --from names
  another.

  A binary that cannot be imported is skipped, and the rest carry on: it was not
  built from a released version (a working tree, a modified tree, a replace
  directive), it is not a Go binary, it is already managed, or go could not
  install it. The summary says why for each. Naming a binary that is not in the
  directory is an error (exit 5) once the others are done.

  Examples:
    gotools import-gobin
    gotools import-gobin goimports staticcheck
    gotools import-gobin --all --dry-run
    gotools import-gobin --all --from ~/bin

  Options:
    --from <string>  Directory holding the binaries (default: GOBIN, else GOPATH/bin)
    --all            Import every importable binary
    --dry-run        Show what would be imported without making changes
    --offline        Refuse to import (needs the network), exit 6
